current_evidence: The council's 'apply for planning permission' page still links this Appendix F validation document for all non-householder applications (the separate householder checklist was reviewed and republished in December 2024), and searches found no newer local list or consultation.

issues.detail: List date 2022-05-01 is the planned review date, not the list date. The document (Appendix F, Validation of Planning Applications) applies to validations from July 2020 and replaced a November 2017 version.
issues.evidence: Document applies to validations from July 2020; 'next review ... May 2022'.

issues.detail: Runnymede's own list is July 2020 and overdue for review (it cites NPPF 2019 and predates statutory BNG), though it is still the one the council links. Grokbot does not record the householder validation checklist's own date: first published May 2021, reviewed and republished December 2024.
issues.evidence: Householder checklist: 'initially published in May 2021' ... 'reviewed and republished in December 2024'.

issues.detail: Local requirements in the document that Grokbot did not capture: 10.4 Street scene (proposals adjoining or close to other buildings; for householders: attached dwellings, side extensions, roof alterations, dormers); 12.1-12.3 Green Belt information (extensions, replacement and new buildings with original building details, floorspace and cross-sections; infilling/redevelopment statement on footprint, floorspace and hardstanding); 19 Green and Blue Infrastructure Checklist (all development, proportionate for householder); 20.2 Construction Transport Management Plan (major); 26 Open Space Statement (loss of open space); 29 Contaminated Land Assessment (contamination known or suspected, or vulnerable use); 33 Groundwater / water quality assessment (EIA development; basements where the water table is high); 35 Utilities Framework (more than 50 dwellings); 42 Site Waste Management Plan (recommended for majors); 43 Microclimate Assessment (tall buildings over 25m); 44 Wind turbines (11m or higher, or rotor over 2m: MOD letter, noise and air traffic information).

Several application-type rows say '(none)' although the document sets type-specific requirements: Lawful development cert (item 41, full supporting evidence for Certificate of Lawfulness); Works to trees (item 45, site plan showing tree positions, details of and reasons for works, replanting details for felling); Demolition in conservation area (item 24, justification statement for demolition in a CA); Change of use - prior approval (item 13, plans and technical evidence such as noise, flood, structural or contamination reports, depending on the procedure). Outline is also '(none)' though general items (DAS for major, FRA, AH statement, etc.) apply to it.
issues.evidence: Item 41 'Certificate of Lawfulness Evidence'; item 45 'Works to Trees (TPOs and Conservation Areas)'; item 13 'Prior Approval Applications'.

issues.detail: The Householder rows leave out items on the householder checklist: Tree Survey / Arboricultural Statement (applications that could affect trees within or outside the site, or a TPO); Heritage statement and Archaeology study (listed or locally listed building, conservation area, Area of High Archaeological Potential); Design and access statement (over 100 sqm in a conservation area); Existing and proposed street views (raising eaves/ridge and visible from the street).
issues.evidence: Householder checklist items 'Tree Survey/Arboricultural Statement', 'Heritage statement and Archaeology study', 'Design and access statement'.

issues.detail: Householder trigger excerpts are jumbled. 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' mixes Part 1 notice, cross-section and FRA-template text, whereas the checklist requires cross sections for 'properties within the Green Belt'. The FRA row says only 'a simple Flood Risk Assessment may be required' (from the web page), whereas the checklist trigger is Flood Zones 2 and 3. The Block plan, CIL and Roof plan rows have fee-schedule and Planning Portal text spliced in.
issues.evidence: Checklist: Cross sections - 'Planning applications for properties within the Green Belt'; FRA template - 'Planning applications located within flood zones 2 and 3'.

issues.detail: Many Full planning trigger excerpts are fragments that drop the thresholds: Affordable Housing (10 or more net additional units); Air Quality (within 70m of or next to an AQMA, or proposals affecting air quality); Energy and Sustainability (major development; 1,000 sqm+ net additional floorspace must meet 10% from renewables/low carbon); Arboricultural and Transport Assessment (both use the same generic 'to ensure consistency' sentence instead of 'trees on or adjacent to the site that could be affected' / 'where traffic or pedestrian movements are created'); Planning Obligations ('a bespoke section 106 agreement.'); BNG ('...may need to be submitted. 23.'); Telecommunications ('with the ICNIRP guidelines is required.').

The Drainage Strategy / SuDS excerpt comes from the FRA section ('address the requirement for safe access...'). The actual item 18 Sustainable Drainage Statement is required for all major applications and recommended for non-major ones, excluding changes of use and householder development.

The Retail / Town Centre Impact row quotes generic NPPF sequential-approach text. The local trigger is retail over 500 sqm, or other main town centre uses over 2,500 sqm, outside Addlestone, Chertsey and Egham town centres.

The Thames Basin Heaths SPA requirement is captured without its trigger. The HRA row and the tab item mention the SANGS/SAMM Unilateral Undertaking and 50+ dwellings at 5-7km, but omit the core trigger: residential sites 400m to 5km from the SPA must provide the UU before validation.
issues.evidence: Item 14.2: applies to sites 400m to 5km from the SPA; UU covering SANGS and SAMM needed before validation.

issues.detail: Two rows are mislabelled. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' holds the town-centre retail sequential test text (item 28), not the flood sequential test. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' holds arboricultural method statement / tree text (item 23).
issues.evidence: Excerpts: 'must apply a sequential test to planning applications for main town centre uses...'; 'arboricultural method statement details for any proposed development activities ... within RPAs'.

issues.detail: Marketing Report is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval'. The source applies it to planning applications for loss or change of use of a public house, loss of employment or retail use, or demolition of a heritage asset, not to prior approval notifications.
issues.evidence: Item 39: 'may be required for any application proposing the loss or change of use of a public house...'.

issues.detail: 26 Full planning rows are 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning' (e.g. Air Quality, Ecology, FRA, Travel Plan), although Appendix F applies to all non-householder application types. Telecommunications (mast/antenna applications by operators, often prior approval) is under Full planning only. DAS is missing from Listed building consent, although item 6(c) requires it for LBC.
issues.evidence: Item 6: DAS required for '(c) listed building consent'; item 40 Telecommunications.

issues.detail: Tab items and rows include fragments and context, not requirements: 'The Highways Agency also provides advice for the siting of wind turbines at 37412/dft-circular-strategic-road.pdf 45 Applications for Works to Trees e.g.'; 'Part of the Borough is covered by the London and South West Water Bodies SPA'; 'In addition adjoining the western boundary of the Borough is the TBHSPA'; drawing items ending with stray numbers ('... 1.', '... 10.'); 'The pl an c an be hand drawn...', which is garbled and belongs to item 45 Works to Trees, not general drawing standards. The 'Pre-application advice / engagement details' row is also a fragment ('part of pre-application discussions to avoid delays...').
'Daylight / Sunlight / Overshadowing Assessment' and 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' are both taken from the single item 34 Sunlight and Daylight Assessment.

The Crime prevention excerpt runs into the next item ('...99 16 37 Lighting Assessment Technical lighting details...'). It also omits the trigger: crime in the DAS where a DAS is required, and a separate statement for uses linked to anti-social behaviour such as wine bars and night clubs.

summary: Grokbot's link is the council's current non-householder validation document, but it dates from July 2020 (not May 2022, which is the overdue review date). About a dozen local requirements are missing, including Green Belt statements, street scene, contaminated land, Green and Blue Infrastructure checklist, wind turbines, LDC and tree-works evidence. Many triggers are fragments that lose their thresholds, and several rows are mislabelled or put under the wrong application type.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
